messages:
incident-bot: Paging: KV-cache tail-latency SLO breach (p95 > 450ms) across us-west-2 pods. Alert: kv-cache:latency.p95 > 450ms for 3m, continuous-batching queue depth spike. Pager: maya.

maya (oncall): on it. grabbing logs + rolling through runbook now. @jonas can you join? this smells like the continuous-batching regression from the last rollout.

jonas (eng-runtime): joining. saw the alert, thanks. quick read: p50 fine, p95/p99 exploded, batch sizes show bimodal distribution (small interactive requests + huge long-context requests). suspected fairness issue in batch scheduler for KV-prefetch paths. pulling metrics: 

jonas (eng-runtime): metrics snippet: 
```
kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.62 -> 0.40 (10:12 -> 10:18)
batch_scheduler_queue_depth: median 6 -> 48
batch_size_p95: 512 -> 2048
latency_p95_tokens: 120ms -> 520ms
```

priya (sre): that hit-rate drop + queue depth increase -> eviction thrash on KV cache? but logs show large numbers of partial KV prefetch evictions. also seeing a lot of long-running "long-doc" requests pinning batches. we should throttle continuous prefetch batching for KV paths immediately.

maya (oncall): customer-impact? laura?

laura (support): no 500s reported yet, but a handful of top-tier customers reported degraded interactive latency in the last 20m. I opened a ticket for one enterprise account — they're seeing chat responses hang ~2-3s. I'll keep updating.

jonas (eng-runtime): proposed hotfix (fast mitigation): 1) temporarily disable continuous KV prefetch batching flag; 2) enable fair_queueing on batch-scheduler for mixed workloads; 3) lower max_batch_size for KV-path to 1024. I can push a config patch to canary then roll.

priya (sre): +1. also increase autoscale target for kv-cache pods by +25% to buy headroom while we patch.

jonas (eng-runtime): creating patch now. patch includes: 
```
# patch: batch-scheduler config
continuous_kv_prefetch: false
batch_scheduler:
  fairness: true
  kv_path:
    max_batch_size: 1024
    prefetch_window_ms: 50
```

jonas (eng-runtime): applying to canary cluster (kv-cache-canary) with rolling restart. watch logs for eviction rate and batch_queue_depth.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: config-change-1773456795 -> kv-cache/canary (jonas). CI checks passed.

jonas (eng-runtime): canary up. immediate signal: batch_queue_depth dropped from 48 -> 10, p95 latency dropped from 520ms -> 210ms within 40s. kv cache eviction rate down 70%.

priya (sre): eyes on autoscaler — scaled kv-cache pods +25% as requested. No new OOMs.

laura (support): reporting back to affected customers: two customers saw noticeable improvement after 60s of canary hitting; ticket owners acknowledged. I'll mark incidents as degraded->partial on our status page.

carl (eng-platform): should we stage this to prod rollout? we need to be careful: the fairness toggle could increase latency for pure long-batch workloads. recommend gradual rollout with monitoring on both latency and throughput.

jonas (eng-runtime): agreed. starting progressive rollout to 30% prod pool now, will pause at 5 min if any metric regresses.

deploy-bot: Rollout: config-change-1773456795 -> kv-cache/prod (30%).

jonas (eng-runtime): rollout stable at 30% after 3m. p95 across rolled nodes ~200-260ms, global p95 trending down. no errors.

maya (oncall): I'll keep the incident paged while we watch for 20m. Priya, can you capture heap/eviction profiles for postmortem? Jonas, please paste the exact flags you toggled in the runbook.

priya (sre): collecting heapdumps now and making a small trace sample of KV eviction cycles for the timeline.

jonas (eng-runtime): adding to runbook: 
```
- continuous_kv_prefetch -> false (temporary)
- batch_scheduler.fairness -> true
- kv_path.max_batch_size -> 1024
- autoscale_target += 25% (kv-cache autoscaler)
- Observe: eviction_rate, batch_queue_depth, p95
```

laura (support): support notes: affected customers list: ENT-342, PLG-88 (high priority). both acknowledged improvement. I'll follow up postmortem with any customer notes for comms.

priya (sre): checklist for after stabilization: 1) revert autoscale bump if not needed, 2) collect perf traces, 3) schedule postmortem w/ eng-runtime and platform, 4) consider longer-term fix: smarter batch sharding or request-weighted fairness.

jonas (eng-runtime): observed tail latency cliff is reproducible locally with replaying mixed workload (long + short). root cause hypothesis: continuous prefetching allowed large requests to monopolize kernel/kv cache insert paths because the scheduler's batching window favored filling large batches, starving small interactive requests. fairness toggle enforces round-robin-ish selection. need better heuristics for mixed workloads.

maya (oncall): p95 stabilized under 300ms for 15m. eviction rate down and no new customer complaints. I'm going to close the page and open an incident ticket for a full postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident status -> mitigated by configuration hotfix (continuous_kv_prefetch disabled + fairness enabled). Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-batch-fairness. Postmortem ticket: INC-2026-1783 created.

maya (oncall): final notes: owners: jonas (root cause + runtime fix), priya (SRE data + mitigation cert), carl (platform follow-ups), laura (customer comms). action items in ticket: implement weighted fair scheduler, add canary tests for mixed workloads, add alerting on batch queue fairness metric.

jonas (eng-runtime): I'll draft the postmortem and include reproducer + perf tests. thanks all for quick coordination. :thumbsup:

laura (support): leaving a note for customer comms: will prepare an update to impacted customers after postmortem.

maya (oncall): closing thread in 10. thanks team. :white_check_mark:
